title: connection blackout guard and progressive SLO rearm (hotfix)
author: Ethan Li
release_notes: Hotfix: add connection blackout guard and progressive SLO rearm. Improves graceful degradation during sudden connection floods and reduces oscillation on circuit reopen. Backported to 2026-02 patch release.
description: Context: A customer incident exposed a rapid connection-flood scenario that caused local circuit flip-flopping and a cascade of tenant-level SLO violations. This PR introduces a lightweight "blackout guard" and a progressive SLO rearm policy to reduce oscillation and give regional failover time to stabilize. Motivation: keep user-facing latency SLOs stable during short congestion spikes, avoid aggressive tenant eviction, and ensure repairability without manual intervention. Summary of changes: || 1) runtime: add connection_blackout_detector that tracks short-lived burst profiles per route/tenant and emits a local 'blackout' status to the node-level circuit manager. Blackout state prevents immediate circuit reopen for a configurable cooloff window and increases local prioritization thresholds. || 2) slo_rearm: replace binary rearm with progressive rearm stages (probe -> soft-rearm -> full-rearm). Each stage has telemetry gates and backoff timers so we avoid full reopens on transient success. || 3) telemetry: new metrics (runtime.blackout_events_total, runtime.blackout_duration_seconds, slo.rearm_stage_total, slo.rearm_probe_success_rate) and tracing spans to help incident diagnosis. || 4) config: expose new per-tenant knobs in runtime config (blackout_threshold_per_minute, blackout_cooloff_seconds, rearm_probe_ttl, rearm_stage_backoffs) and sensible defaults that preserve existing behavior for customers who don't opt in. || 5) tests: unit tests for blackout detector logic and integration tests that simulate connection bursts and validate rearm hysteresis. Also added a quick canary script used by SRE to exercise the flow in staging. Changeset summary, commits and high-level file diffs are below.

review_comments: Maya Kapoor: Overall looks good; two concerns: ensure default cooloff is not too long for low-volume tenants and add a unit test that asserts we don't block reopen forever.
Author (Ethan Li): Addressed. Shortened default cooloff to 30s for tenants below 20 rps and added TestBlackoutNotPermanent in blackout_detector_test.go. See commit d9a8c77.
Nina Patel: Telemetry looks useful, but add an open / close event tag to the blackout metric to make dashboards easier.
Author (Ethan Li): Added event_type label for open/close to runtime.blackout_events_total; updated docs and alerts accordingly.
Carlos Gomez: Can we gate the rearm probe traffic so it doesn't magnify the burst? Suggest probe rate limit tied to circuit weight.
Author (Ethan Li): Implemented probe rate limiting with a token-bucket sized by circuit weight. Added integration test to validate behavior under bursty probe scenarios.

canary_run_summary: Staging canary executed 2026-02-16 against a synthetic 10s burst profile. Observed reduced reopen churn: reopen attempts decreased 82% during bursts and overall SLO violations dropped 61% in the window. No regressions in median latency.
rollback_plan: Backout: revert merge commit and roll forward with previous runtime binary; additional mitigation is to set blackout_threshold_per_minute to a very high value via tenant config to disable detection while investigation proceeds.
notes_for_ops: Ops: new alerts added runtime.blackout_events_total > 10 in 1m for any region triggers Sev3. If noise observed, tune blackout_threshold_per_minute per-tenant. Use staging-canary/blackout_smoke.sh to validate behavior in a controlled window.
